lore.from: Slavic folklore: Poland (domowik), Russia (domovoi), Ukraine (domovyk), Belarus (damavik), Czechia (děd), Slovakia (škriatok), Bulgaria (stopan)
lore.title: The Domowiki
lore.eyebrow: Slavic folklore · Poland and its neighbours
story: Somewhere behind your stove, in the warmest, darkest corner of the house, lives a little old man with a huge nose and a beard down to his toes. You will never see him. But he sees you.

He is a Domowik, the spirit of the home, and in the villages of Poland and the lands around it, every house had one. People believed he was the family's first grandfather, still looking after his children's children long after his own time. He kept thieves and bad luck outside, watched the babies at night, and slipped out to the stable to braid the manes of the horses he liked.

Keeping him happy was easy. A slice of bread with a pinch of salt, a bowl of porridge, a little milk by the stove, and a home without shouting: that was all he asked. Forget him, or fill the house with quarrels, and the pots would clang at night, tools would go missing, and sleepers woke with their hair in knots.

If you felt his hand in the dark, everyone knew what it meant. Warm and furry: good times ahead. Cold: trouble coming. And when a family moved house, they never left him behind. They carried a glowing ember from the old stove, or an old worn shoe, and said out loud: "Grandfather, come with us to the new home."
facts: The name means 'the one of the house'. Every home had its own Domowik, often thought to be the family's first ancestor.
He usually looks like a small old man with a grey beard and a coat of soft fur. Some said he could look like the head of the family, or take the shape of a cat.
He lives behind or under the stove, or under the threshold, and looks after the family, the children and the animals.
Families left him bread and salt, porridge or milk, and good behaviour: he hates quarrels, swearing and a messy home.
An angry Domowik bangs pots, hides tools, pinches sleepers and tangles hair. A very unhappy one leaves, and the house loses its luck.
Moving house, families carried embers from the old stove, or an old shoe, and asked him along: 'Grandfather, come with us to the new home.'
He braids the manes of the horses he likes and tires out the ones he doesn't.
A warm, furry hand touching you at night was a sign of good times ahead; a cold one, of trouble.
He has relatives: the Dvorovoi of the yard, the Bannik of the bathhouse, the Ovinnik of the barn, and in some tales a wife, the Kikimora or Domowicha.
Folklorists describe the Domowik as the household's own piece of Rod, the Slavic god of kin and ancestors: each family's first forefather, still looking after his descendants.
Families often called him 'grandfather' (Polish dziadek, or fondly dziadziuś), never by name, out of respect.
He had a wife, the Domovikha (also Domania), who liked to live in the cellar. Some writers say she was the original house spirit, and he came later.
The Domowik could take the shape of a snake living under the threshold or behind the stove. Whoever harmed that house snake harmed the family's luck.
The Ovinnik kept the drying barn, where the grain was dried over a fire. He had to be given offerings, or he might burn the barn down.
In Polish lore the Kłobuk looks like a soaked, bedraggled chick sitting on a fence. Take it home and feed it, and it brings grain and riches into the house.

cards.name: Dziadziuś, Heart of the House
cards.flavor: The smallest Domowik in the house. Everyone listens to him anyway.

kitten.name: Dziadziuś, Heart of the House
kitten.text:
Exhaust: Ready one of your Offerings.
Awaken: You have 8 or more Offerings.

bigCat.name: Dziadziuś, Master of the House
bigCat.text: Fierce. Exhaust: Ready two of your Offerings.

cards.name: Stove Keeper
cards.text: Hello: Ready one of your Offerings.
cards.flavor: Keeps the embers warm until morning.

cards.name: Moving-Day Domowik
cards.flavor: Carry the old fire, and the home comes with you.

cards.name: Mane-Braiding Domowik
cards.flavor: The horse he favours wakes with braids in its mane.

cards.name: Keeper of the Door
cards.flavor: Nothing crosses the threshold without his nod.

cards.name: Ovinnik of the Drying Barn
cards.flavor: Keeps the fire that dries the grain. Feed him first, or no one gets bread.

cards.name: Bread-and-Salt Greeter
cards.text: Hello: Heal 2 from each unit you control.
cards.flavor: Every guest is welcome. Every crumb is counted.

cards.name: Kikimora, the Night Spinner
cards.text: Hello: If you're Well-Fed, draw 2 cards.
cards.flavor: Spins by the stove all night. The yarn tells tomorrow.

cards.name: Dvorovoi, Lord of the Yard
cards.flavor: The house belongs to his cousin. Everything outside is his.

cards.name: Bowl of Kasha
cards.flavor: A bowl by the stove, the first spoonful for him.

cards.name: A Domowik's Temper
cards.text: Lucky. Deal 5 damage to a unit.
cards.flavor: Slam a door in his house and he slams back.

cards.name: Saucer of Milk
cards.text: Ambush. A unit you control gets +2 Power this round. Ready one of your Offerings.
cards.flavor: Warm milk in the stable keeps the whole barn happy.

cards.name: Old Bast Shoe
cards.text: Attached unit gets +2 Power and +2 Health.
cards.flavor: His ride to every new home.

cards.name: Domowik in a Cat's Shape
cards.flavor: The family cat sleeps in the stove corner. Or does it?

cards.name: Babunia, Lady of the Cellar
cards.text: Guardian. Hello: Ready one of your Offerings.
cards.flavor: Some say she was the first spirit of the house. He only moved in later.

cards.name: Bannik of the Bathhouse
cards.flavor: Always leave the last steam for him.

cards.name: Hearth Cricket
cards.flavor: Sings behind the stove, where the Domowik sleeps.

cards.name: The House Snake
cards.flavor: Lives under the doorstep. Harm it, and the family's luck goes with it.

cards.name: Kłobuk, the Soggy Chick
cards.flavor: Found shivering on the fence in the rain. Take it in, and it brings things home.

cards.name: Warm Hand in the Night
cards.text: Ambush. A unit you control gets +2 Power this round.
cards.flavor: A soft, warm, furry hand on your cheek means good luck.

cards.name: Knotted Mane
cards.flavor: Anger the Domowik and wake up with tangled hair.

domowiki.name: Domowiki
domowiki.blurb: Feed the house spirits, then wake the giants. Gather extra Offerings; at 7 or more, the Domowiki are Well-Fed.
